newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian govt wants more Gazprom say.
newsitem.headline: Russian govt wants more Gazprom say.

text.p: First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov said on Friday that the Russian government should reassert its role in running the state gas monopoly, RAO Gazprom, Interfax news agency said.

Nemtsov, appointed by President Boris Yeltsin last month with a brief to reform Russia's so-called natural monopolies, said that of the state's 40 percent stake in Gazprom, a 35 percent packet was controlled by a structure run by the firm's management.
"It's essential we change this situation," Interfax quoted the first deputy premier as saying.
Nemtsov may face resistance from powerful industrial lobbies. They see Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, a former head of Gazprom, as a guarantor of their interests.

The communist-dominated State Duma voted a non-binding resolution on Friday urging Yeltsin to halt plans to reform the natural monopolies, including Gazprom. The deputies accused the government of planning to break up and privatise the group.
Nemtsov told Interfax "no one is going to break Gazprom up into pieces". He said, however, that Gazprom ought to pay its debts to the federal government and national pension fund.
One goal of restructuring Gazprom should be the provision of a single transport tariff for all gas producers, Nemtsov said.
The company should also have to face competition for rights to exploit new reserves.
Nemtsov also said Russia had no intention of privatising or breaking up the UES national electricity network.
He said that restructuring UES should create "free access to the energy transport arteries" and competition between generators in a new wholesale electricity market.
